title: refactor(cli): decouple ToolGroupMessage from internal type guards and payload structures

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue clearly identifies a specific code design flaw in ToolGroupMessage.tsx (lines 79-81) where UI code is tightly coupled to core payload structures via type guards like isFileDiff. It provides actionable details for refactoring.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Decoupling tool payload type checking from UI components requires refactoring result metadata and adapter/formatting layer across packages/core and packages/cli.

summary.problem: ToolGroupMessage component directly uses internal type guards (such as isFileDiff) and checks raw object shapes to determine if a compact tool has a dense payload.
summary.root_cause: The hasDensePayload helper in ToolGroupMessage.tsx inspects internal core result structures directly rather than relying on a result metadata property or dedicated adapter.
summary.context: UI components should remain decoupled from internal tool payload structures to keep the UI layer clean and maintainable.

steps: Add explicit metadata (e.g. hasDensePayload property) or an abstraction on ToolResultDisplay / IndividualToolCallDisplay for identifying dense payloads.
Update tool result adapters or creation logic to populate this metadata flag when constructing display objects.
Refactor hasDensePayload in ToolGroupMessage.tsx to rely on the metadata/adapter property instead of invoking isFileDiff or inspecting raw payload object keys directly.
Remove unused core type guard imports (like isFileDiff) from ToolGroupMessage.tsx.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: ToolGroupMessage correctly identifies compact tools with dense payloads using the decoupled result metadata without importing or calling internal core type guards.
verification_steps: Run vitest on packages/cli/src/ui/components/messages/ToolGroupMessage.compact.test.tsx to ensure compact rendering remains identical.
Verify that tool calls with file diffs and summary/payload structures continue to be rendered as dense payloads.
